STANDING RULES (full text in the archive, search the quoted title):
- Lock protocol: a lane writes a lock line (Lane, UTC time, what, tier) before a push, then the pushed and look-done lines, then the release line, in the format used by the entries below. No production read, even read only, while any lock is open.
- "THE TIERED PREPUSH RULE": FULL tier for engine and data files (scripts/engineDataFiles.mjs), FAST for the rest. Never push over a failing prePush.
- "STANDING RULE FOR EVERY LANE: one archive load at a time": no two lanes run prePush, a results table, a cold test or a chain at once.
- Efficiency rules (Sam, Oct 21): Lane C is the batch integrator, pushes at most once an hour; lane reports are three lines; Lane F reports only when something needs Sam or something landed.
- One engine (oneEngineAnswer), pages compute nothing. No secrets in chat, files or logs. No em or en dashes. Every report ends with a Search check line.

STAGE 1. SHELL AND RENAME

STAGE 2. THE FOUR START PAGES (match the images, with these changes)
- Headlines in the existing serif, not the sans in the images. Same input component, size, microphone and submit on all four.
- Home (/): remove the redirect to /sell. "WELCOME TO GOASKSAM", "Find the car you're looking for.", "Tell Sam what you want. - WHAT "NEW" MEANS: a live car that matches the Task and is not in task.reported_ids (the last 500 ids reported for that Task) and is newer than the Task's checkpoint. A car reported once, in the opening update or any later one, is never reported again for that Task. Only after 500 further reports could an id fall off the list, and the checkpoint still keeps it out unless the listing itself is newer.

The engine's model list for a brand, for the Task model question (replaces lib/tasks/tasks.js modelOptions for a brand with no model). IMPORT: `import { modelChoicesForBrand } from "../onebox.js";` (lib/onebox.js). CALL: `await modelChoicesForBrand(env, make, years)`. env = `{ supabaseUrl, supabaseKey }` (the engine's env, as oneEngineAnswer takes). make = the brand as typed or resolved ("Porsche", "Land Rover", "Mercedes-Benz"). years = optional `{ yearMin, yearMax }` (either may be null or missing): when given, the list holds only models sold in those years; if that leaves nothing it is the brand's whole list. Nothing else filters it (not colour, not what is on sale). RETURNS `{ make, options: [ { label, value, n, any } ... ] }`: up to SIX model entries, most-sold first (`label` and `value` are the model name as Find prints it, `n` = archive sales in the last 3 years, `any:false`), then ONE last entry `{ label: "Any Porsche", value: null, n: null, any: true }`. A brand with no models (unknown, read failed) returns just the Any entry. It reads the same list Find and Market Check offer for a bare brand (topModelsForMake: chassis codes collapsed, 996/997 are 911, base models), so Find and Tasks agree. Offline check scripts/modelChoicesCheck.mjs (in prePush).   FIELD SHAPES (on the raw engine answer, on the mapped answer from mapEngineAnswer, and on the stored core from coreOf; both null when the answer has no pool or nothing clears):
  best_day = { day: "Sunday", count: 5, n: 13, measure: "median_vs_pool_median_pct", lead_pct: 29.3, median: 40200, pool_median: 31100, margin: 32.2, fence: { min_sales: 5, min_margin: 5 }, window: { months: 12, from: "YYYY-MM-DD", to: "YYYY-MM-DD" } }. Result tier only. Measure: the day's median price against the pool median, in percent. A day needs 5 sales; the winner sits above the pool median and leads the next ranked day by 5 points or more (margin is the real lead in points); fewer than two ranked days is null. dayBuckets is untouched.
  reserve_split = { winner: "reserve" | "no_reserve" | "none", a: { side: "no_reserve", n, median }, b: { side: "reserve", n, median }, n, gap_pct, scope_label: "2005 to 2012 911 Carrera", window: { months, from, to } }. Walks the page's own pool, then the generation (the spec's own year bounds, same trim), then the model in every year, no trim; stops at the first scope where both sides hold 8 sales; same window as the range and the same price fence. Cars with an unknown reserve flag are left out. winner is the side with the higher median when the gap (over the lower median) is 5 percent or more, else "none". Result and thin tiers; the walk reads the archive only on a result tier and only when the answer is under 6 s old, so a slow answer never waits for it.
  STAMP: stored answers key on the stamp, so e90 answers are stale after the bump and carry no fields until the full warm rewrites them; the warm must finish before a card can show either field. - REASON LINE TABLE (Lane B, Oct 28, e99-20261028-trimfix, lib/reasonWords.js; every producer builds its line there, no page writes one; check scripts/reasonWordsCheck.mjs). Before and after, one per line, [id | before | after]:
    thin.house_share | BEFORE: The sales of this car are too one-sided to mark a range from. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: These sales come mostly from one place, so no range is shown.
    thin.few_sales | BEFORE: Not enough sales of this exact car to give a reliable range. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: Too few sales to show a range.
    thin.mixed_prices | BEFORE: These sales sit in very different price ranges, so no typical range is shown. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: These sales sit in very different price ranges, so no range is shown.
    thin.pooled_apart | BEFORE: These sales split into options that sit in different price ranges, so no one typical range is shown. Pick an option below to read its own sales. | AFTER: These sales split into options priced apart, so pick one to see its range.
    thin.few_comparable | BEFORE: Too few of these sales can be compared side by side to give a reliable range. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: Too few of these sales match closely enough to show a range.
    wide.mileage | BEFORE: Wide because 20,000 to 90,000 miles. Add yours. | AFTER: The range is wide because mileage runs from 20,000 to 90,000 miles.
    wide.year | BEFORE: Wide because these run from 2008 to 2014. Pick a year. | AFTER: The range is wide because the cars run from 2008 to 2014.

- FOR LANE E, matchedOption shape at ENGINE READY 6 (Lane B, Oct 28): an OBJECT, not a label and not an index. matchedOption = { dimension: "gearbox"|"body"|"edition"|"mileage", value, label, n, low, high, line, inHeadline, refine } or null when the title names no option. Print matchedOption.label for the name ("PDK") and matchedOption.line for the whole line; the matched option is also options[0] and optionLines[0] (the engine reorders them, so a page that prints the list in the order sent leads with it, and never searches for the match). inHeadline false means the match is a chip of another dimension: low, high and line are null, send matchedOption.refine to get its figures. Example, 2014 Porsche Boxster S PDK on the Find card: matchedOption {"dimension":"gearbox","value":"auto","label":"PDK","n":10,"low":32500,"high":35500,"line":"PDK $32,500 to $35,500, 10 sales","inHeadline":true,"refine":{"tx":"auto"}}, options [PDK, Manual], optionLines ["PDK $32,500 to $35,500, 10 sales","Manual $34,500 to $37,500, 10 sales"]. Fields: m.matchedOption, m.options, m.optionLines on the Find card; raw.matchedOption on a Market Check answer.

- FOLLOW-UP 1b, WHAT ROTATING BREAKS: the production service role key is read by every Vercel function, every GitHub Actions job (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY secret) and the lanes' scripts. Rotating Supabase's JWT secret changes the service and the public (anon) key together; change both in Vercel and in the GitHub secret, redeploy once, and expect brief errors until both are set. Rotating the OldCarsData key means the Vercel variable, the GitHub secret OLDCARSDATA_API_KEY and the nightly ingest and warm. The other project's key breaks only whatever uses that project (not the product). The tester-code links die when CURTAIN_TESTER_CODE is rotated, which is already on the launch eve list. Nothing here is needed for the site to run: the allow rules can simply be deleted.

- FOLLOW-UP 2, HOW THE KEY TRAVELS (Lane F, 17:38Z, origin/main 48c8f680, for Lane D's stage 1 gate): (a) Vercel crons: no key in any path in vercel.json (none carries key, secret or token); Vercel adds Authorization: Bearer CRON_SECRET itself. Routes accept it through lib/_credential.js hasServerCredential or the cronOk-style compares listed in the sweep. (b) GitHub nightly (.github/workflows/nightly.yml, copy in docs/nightly-workflow.yml): the premium job sends PROBE_KEY as an x-ops-key HEADER, fed to curl from stdin (-H @-) so it is not in the process list. (c) scripts/warm.js sends x-probe-key as a HEADER, with warm:true as a plain body flag and an optional x-vercel-protection-bypass header; warmNamed.mjs, warmUnion.mjs and about 59 other scripts send x-ops-key (or x-probe-key) as a HEADER. (d) No script, workflow or lib sends the key in an address. (e) ONE sender puts it in a request BODY: scripts/buyTimes.mjs line 113 (action explain, field key), the caller of the buySearch b.key path. Nobody else calls the landing, finds, ladder or test send actions, so closing the body path only needs buyTimes.mjs changed to its header (it already sends x-ops-key on its page requests). keyInAddressCheck.mjs proves the server refuses addresses. The Bearer CRON_SECRET form is sent only by Vercel itself, never by a script.

- TYPED EQUALS VIN GATE (Lane B, Oct 28), code cbc27d22 on lane-b-e96-fix, no stamp change, NOT pushed: ops task vintyped (read only: the stored VIN identities of the nightly rollout, the resolver and the stored Market Check rows; no visitor-path read, no address cap, no writes, no OldCarsData). It takes up to 50 stored identities, always the 996 when one is stored, and compares the identity a VIN page hands the engine with the typed name's resolution (lib/vinTyped.js): the same stored answer key, or the same tier, count, range, rung and options state. Returns checked, identical, differ, go (true only when every pair is identical), the first ten differences and the 996 flag. GO when differ is 0 and checked is 50; NO-GO otherwise, the differing pairs name the field. scripts/vinTypedCheck.mjs (own check, registered in prePush): the offline fixture of five real identities including two 996 shapes reads the same key typed and by identity; a pair with different keys and no stored answer, or a different count, is NO-GO and names the field; the check fails on the tree without the module. The live number comes from running the task after this push. All 268 checks: the same 8 baseline failures, none new.

- CHART LADDER, STAGE 1 AND THE FIELD SHAPE FOR LANE E (Lane B, Oct 28). STAGE 1: yes, it is computed at read time from the stored answer's own sales (rawPool, full rows with date and price) like matchedOption: NO stored answer change, NO stamp bump. One honest limit: the stored answer holds the window the answer reads (12, 24 or 36 months), not the wider 36 month chart set, so scoped candles need three candles of 5 sales of ONE option inside that window and will land less often than the pooled chart; dots land on everything else. Carrying the 36 month chart rows in the stored answer would land more candles but changes stored answers (a stamp decision, e100); I have NOT done it. FIELD SHAPE, on every result and thin answer as answer.chart (raw.chart), settled: chart = { type: "candles" | "dots" | "withheld", scope: null | { dimension, value, label, line }, size: "quarter"|"half-year"|"year"|null, spanLabel: string|null, caption: string|null, note: string|null, buckets: [{ period, label, low, high, typical, count }] | null, dots: [{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", price: 12345, option: "PDK"|null }] | null, withheld: { reason: "too_few", floor: 3, n, line } | null, n }. candles: draw buckets, caption under it, scope.line above it when scope is set (the engine's words: "The candles show the PDK sales only, 24 of the 31."); note is the held-chart sentence ("The mix of cars changed from quarter to quarter, so a change here would not show the market moving.") and prints under the chart when present. dots: draw one dot per sale, date against price, option names each dot (null when the answer has no options), caption "Each dot is one sale, since December 2025.", no line between dots, no trend. withheld: draw nothing, print withheld.line ("Only 2 dated sales, too few to chart, so the sales themselves are listed."). Too few = under 3 dated sales. Pages print these fields and compute nothing; the old d.trend, d.chartCaption and d.trendHeld stay on the answer unchanged.

- LAUNCH DASH AUDIT, STAGE 1, THE ADDRESS AND THE KEY (Lane D, Oct 28): the address is goasksam.com/admin. It has NO dashboard key and no crew code. It answers the plain 404 page to everyone; the page then looks for the signed-in session in the browser (localStorage gas_auth_session) and only an account whose email is in the ADMIN_EMAILS environment variable sees the dashboard drawn in place. Every data call carries that person's sign-in token in a header, nothing in the address. So on his phone Sam: opens goasksam.com, signs in with the Google account whose email is in ADMIN_EMAILS (the sign-in bar on any page; while the site is held he enters the crew link once first, at goasksam.com/api/crew), then opens goasksam.com/admin in the same browser. USAGE_DASHBOARD_KEY is NOT read by anything any more (api/usageDashboard.js line 3 and 6488; LAUNCH EVE 8 deletes it), so rotating or deleting it changes nothing for Sam. The write-capable credentials are PROBE_KEY and OPS_KEY (the x-ops-key header our scripts and lanes use, which also read /api/admin parts check, door, refresh_now); rotating them locks out our scripts only, never Sam's phone. What can lock Sam out: (1) ADMIN_EMAILS not holding the address he signs in with (I cannot read Vercel env; look once tonight), (2) his sign-in session ending (fix: sign in again), (3) rotating Supabase's JWT secret, which signs everyone out (not on the list). After any rotation his steps are the same: open goasksam.com, sign in with Google, open goasksam.com/admin. The crew code rotation ends his crew cookie only; he re-enters the new code at goasksam.com/api/crew and the dashboard is unaffected. No key was printed.

THRESHOLDS, last 60 minutes, real visitors only (crew only if the box is ticked): ACT NOW at 5 or more 5xx, or 3 or more failed searches that are 20 percent or more of the searches, or 5 or more busy line shown, or 3 or more Task emails failed, or a cold 95th at 30 seconds or more; WATCH at 1 5xx, 1 failed search, 1 busy line, 5 limits hit, 1 Task email failed, a cold 95th at 20 seconds, a cold median at 8 seconds, or the newest stored answer older than 36 hours, or when the hour could not be read (the strip never says GOOD on a number it could not read); cold speed counts only with 5 or more cold answers; limits hit never make ACT NOW (a limit is the protection working). Cold limits sit above the recorded history (median about 3.9 s, 95th about 16.3 s, the One Box latency gate). Stored answers not stored today are shown but do not move the strip (they are all off-day each evening Pacific). launchHealthCheck 96 pass (fails on origin/main: no health file; with the unread hour mapped to GOOD it fails 6), launchDashCheck 153 pass, in prePush.
- LAUNCH DASH AUDIT, STAGE 3, THE DOOR (Lane D, Oct 28): the 20,026 held hits are 503s answered before any engine work (lib/_hold.js, the held_at_door event), 99 percent flagged bots, flat near 1,200 an hour (about 20 a minute across all bots), 20,019 of them on /api/history. Once the door opens those same bots reach real routes. Can they slow real answers? On /api/history, no at that volume: a page is cached at the edge for 120 seconds with 600 more served stale (a 404 for 300), so repeat URLs never reach the function, and the route already has its limit (history_page in lib/_ceilings.js, 60 a minute per device and 120 per address, 1,200 and 3,000 an hour, enforced by lib/_routeLimit.js, crew and our keyed jobs exempt, fail-open if the ledger is slow). What is NOT covered: one bot asking for many different URLs from many addresses is limited per address only, there is no whole-route cap, and the held events carry the route not the URL, so I cannot say how many of the 20,019 were distinct pages. Backstops outside the code: the Vercel firewall and Bot Protection decision (LAUNCH EVE 11). No limit number changed. THE HELD COUNT: it is a 503 with Retry-After counted as held_at_door, never an error (the Errors lines and the new strip read error events only; checked with 500 held visits changing nothing). The range total keeps earlier hits of the same day after the site opens, so I added the line that reads zero by itself: Held in the last hour, and Last held visit. Since launch starts at 7:00 AM Pacific and reads 0 from the first minute.

- CACHE HEADER REPORT, NOTHING CHANGED (Lane C, Oct 29 ~3:05 AM PT, read from the repo and curl -I on the bee760b6 pinned build): (1) STATIC CODE FILES (/js/onebox.js, /js/auth.js, /styles.css, every file in public/): "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate" with an ETag. A browser keeps a copy but must ask Vercel each time; unchanged gives a 304, changed gives the new file. That is safe, it is the Vercel default for public/ and vercel.json sets no override (its only headers block is security headers). The Vercel edge copy (x-vercel-cache HIT, age about an hour) is replaced on every deploy. So a normal reload gets new code from these. (2) THE PAGES (HTML, built by api/*.js): crew, crew-cookie, key, sealed and pre-launch requests get "private, no-store". Once the site is launched, public requests get "public, s-maxage=30" (Market Check, Tasks, spec page), BUT Find (api/buy.js:177) gets s-maxage=600 when not "late" (10 minutes at the edge), /sell next (api/sellNext.js:81) gets "max-age=0, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=3600", and the spec page route (api/specPage.js:87) gets "s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400" (a day of stale). (3) MOST LIKELY CAUSE of "old layout until hard refresh": pages that carry their own CSS and JS inline (Feedback, About, Tasks, the shell) have the layout IN the HTML; a browser or edge copy of that HTML is old until it expires or is revalidated, while the external /js and /styles files revalidate every time, so HTML and external files can come from two different builds for up to the s-maxage above, and the page JS can run against old markup. I did not reproduce Sam's case (pre-launch every page is no-store for crew), so this is the code path, not a measured fact. SMALLEST SAFE FIX (needs Sam's yes, nothing changed): after launch cap Find and sell-next at s-maxage=30 like the other pages and drop the day-long stale-while-revalidate on the spec page to 300; optionally add a build id to the external /js and /styles URLs so HTML and files always come from one build. Pre-launch no change is needed.

Three parts, in the order asked. (1) PENDING CARDS: cause: the Find page asked a pending card again only when its market said stillReading with a retryAfterMs; a card whose ask came back empty or failed (a non-JSON 500, a reply that left the card out, a pending market with no retry hints) kept market undefined and the pending line for ever, until a refresh. Fix (e98de600): every pending card keeps being asked on the engine's own cadence (market.retryAfterMs; with none, the engine's stillReadingMarket values handed to the client, so no number of the page's own) until the engine answers or its wait (waitMaxMs) passes, then it redraws in place; past the limit it prints the engine's own cold.missed line. pendingCardFillCheck (in prePush, 43 pass, Chrome at 1440 and 390, engine stubbed): computing then answer, empty twice, 500 twice, pending without hints, a reply that leaves the card out, never arriving (computing, empty): 14 FAIL without the fix, all pass with it. - HIGHEST PRICE SHOWS THE NEWEST FIVE (Lane E, Nov 1 2026, Sam's live look, goasksam.com/preview?view=b&car=2008 Porsche 911 Carrera S). CAUSE: THE ENGINE, Lane B's lib/onebox.js partnerSalesOf: `else if (order === "price") list = cards.slice();` is the answer's own card order, not a sort by price. On that car the cards are in date order, so "price" returned the same five as "date" and the highest sale ($76,000) was never in them. The PAGE is right: each tab sends its own order (partnerDemoCheck: the price, date and miles tabs send "price", "date" and the typed-mileage read) and prints the five it is given in the order given; it sorts nothing. Date and miles are right (168 cases, below). EXACT FAILING REQUEST (the engine function the endpoint calls, partnerPositionsOf(d, ask), on eleven included sales in date order, one of them $76,000 dated 2026-02-20): ask { order: "price", mileage: null, prices: { starting_bid: 40000 } } -> order "price", placedSales 2026-09-21 $44000, 2026-08-19 $66000, 2026-04-16 $66000, 2026-04-09 $44500, 2026-04-02 $59500 (identical to order "date"). Expected: 2026-02-20 $76000, 2026-08-19 $66000, 2026-04-16 $66000, 2026-04-02 $59500, 2025-12-02 $58000. SAME BUG per option of an apart answer (perOption options use the same function). THE FIX (Lane B's file, one line, tried in a scratch copy only): `else if (order === "price") list = cards.slice().sort((x, y) => (Number(y.price) || 0) - (Number(x.price) || 0) || when(y) - when(x));` (highest first, newer first on a tie). CHECK: scripts/partnerOrderCheck.mjs (Lane E, committed on lane-e-apart, NOT in prePush yet because it is red on the engine as it stands: 120 pass, 48 FAIL, all 48 are order "price" or "price must include the highest sale"): every demo car (DEMO_CARS plus the 2008 Carrera S) x three card arrangements (date, price, archive order) x the three orders, on a single range and on both options of an apart answer, the engine's five against the plain order of its own full set. With the one-line fix in a scratch copy: 168 pass, 0 FAIL. Lane B: land the sort, then add partnerOrderCheck to prePush. NOTE FOR THE SWEEP: the demo cars' real sale sets cannot be read offline (no Lane F gap), so the check runs each demo car's name over a seeded sale set; a live look at the real five per car and order waits for a gap: POST /api/partnerAnswer { q: <car>, order: "price" } and read placedSales[0].price against the range's highest sale.

CAUSE: the failing assertion is the last page one ("the sheet finalises, and every field is locked"). The check clicked a reason, which fires an async save whose response rebuilds the whole sheet, then typed into a textarea handle taken before that rebuild; the rebuild detached it, the keystrokes were lost, the line never reached the server (store log: PUT with reasons but line ""), Finalise was refused "Type the line of reasoning". A CHECK race, the finalise rule is deterministic (45/0 every time once the check is steady). REAL DEFECT FOUND ON THE SAME PATH: the page sent sheet_finalise without flushing the 400 ms debounced save, so a sheet could be sealed from a stale draft (reserve typed or changed inside the window sealed as the OLD value, or refused as empty); also a later patch of another kind in the window replaced the earlier one, and saves could land out of order. FIX (public/js/deskvals.js): patches merge, a sheet's saves run one at a time in order, Finalise waits on flush(); window.__deskVals.settled() for checks. CLASS: any check that holds a puppeteer handle across an action that re-renders (found 3 more: deskRailCheck line 53, pdfLayoutCheck 69 to 72); helpers press/typeIn/settle in scripts/deskValsRender.mjs act inside one page turn. - READY B lane-b-tierjob (Lane B, Nov 5 2026, branch lane-b-tierjob from origin/main 57f58fea, NOT pushed; full tip is the commit carrying this line, `git log -1 --format=%H`). THE CONDITION TIER JOB, SAFE FOR THE LIVE SITE. No engine field, no stamp, no stored answer, no warm; the nightly workflow file is a COPY Sam adds. 1. WHY 500 ROWS TOOK 40 TO 66 S. PROVEN FROM THE CODE: the old job read each model's mileage (up to 1000 rows) INSIDE the timed batch, once per new model per run, and it walks in uuid order, so 500 sales meet hundreds of models; the three logged batches fell 66, 48, 41 s on the same 500 rows as the per-run memo filled. Also from the code: the first read had `or=(condition_version is null, neq)`, which cannot use the partial index; the partial index names condition_version, so every update of it is a non-HOT update (all indexes written); a failed model read was stored as "no band" and the sale tiered without its mileage for good; a failed batch read ended the run as "finished". NEEDS SAM'S QUERY (read only, docs/supabase-condition-tier-diagnose.sql blocks 1 to 5): HOT ratio, index count and size, bloat, triggers, other running queries and locks. I cannot say from code how much of the 40 s was the UPDATE. 2. THE JOB NOW: batches of 100, at most 8 new model reads a batch (rows of an unread model wait and are tiered on the next pass with the same tier they would have had), every request aborted at 6 s, a slow batch (over 3 s) doubles the pause, 3 slow batches in a row or one over 15 s STOP the run (exit 0, warning, resumable), a failed model read is never "no band", a failed batch read or write exits 1, --max default 5000 and --minutes default 60. A max, batch, pause or minutes that is not a whole number FAILS (the typed "0 to 500" exits 1 before any read; "0" for max also fails). CPU itself cannot be read from a job; batch time is the proxy. A server side per statement cap is not available through PostgREST without a role wide setting, so the ceiling is the client abort plus the small batch. RESUMABLE AND CANCEL SAFE: each batch is ONE UPDATE (set_condition_tiers), the only write, so a batch lands whole or not at all; a rerun touches only rows not at ct1-20261105 (checked: a failed third write leaves exactly 2 whole batches, the rerun finishes the rest, no row written twice). SCHEDULE: 10:50 UTC (about 3:50 am Pacific): after the 07:11 ingest and the jobs behind it, the 08:00 depth, 09:40/09:50 photo checks and 10:20 admin night refresh, capped at 70 minutes so it ends before the 12:00 fill; concurrency group so two runs never overlap. WHAT SAM RUNS: copy docs/condition-tier-workflow.yml to .github/workflows/condition-tier.yml (replaces the Nov 5 copy), then either let the nightly do the backfill (50,000 rows a night, resumes) or dispatch with batch 100, pause 2000, max 2000000, minutes 70 and repeat until the log says "finished, 0 rows". The 1,500 rows already written stay valid (same version). CHECK scripts/tierJobSafetyCheck.mjs (in prePush, 47 pass); on origin/main code it gives 11 FAIL and then hangs on the unaborted write (exit 13). tierAssignCheck 40, tierPoolCheck 22, sheetReadCheck 149, engineFieldsCheck 12 pass. 3. THE RESULT FOR SENSE. I have NO database key in this environment, so I did NOT read the 1,500 stored rows: the ten samples per tier and the exact Untiered split need Sam's queries C and D and B in docs/supabase-condition-tier-diagnose.sql (one paste back and I tabulate). FROM THE CODE: Untiered means fewer than 3 signals seen. A sale shows a signal only when its text says it; mileage counts only when the model has 20 or more listed odometers; title only when the status says clean or a bad word. The Ferrari houses (Bonhams, Gooding, Broad Arrow, Mecum) carry no description text in the feed, so they can show at most mileage and title: always Untiered, which is honest. Untiered IS honest here (better nothing than a fake number): it stays in the wider pool and out of every same tier pool. Tier 1 needs a score of 4, so four separate good signals; 3 of 1,500 is what that bar gives and is Sam's call. TWO WORDING BUGS I CAN SHOW (not changed, thresholds are Sam's, a change needs a new version ct2): (a) the word "project" alone is a hard negative: "a three-year restoration project completed in 2019 with receipts" and "finished a two year project to restore it, one owner, service records" both come out tier 4 (a finished restoration called a project); (b) "custom" alone counts as a modification: "custom paint to sample, one owner, service records" loses a point. PROPOSAL for Sam: project only as "project car", "a project", "needs restoration", "barn find", "incomplete"; custom only as "custom (wheels|exhaust|intake|...)"; then bump to ct2 and the job reassigns. THRESHOLDS (lib/conditionTier.js, ct1-20261105): mileage at or under the model's lower quartile +1, at or over the upper quartile -1, between 0, needs 20+ listed odometers for the model; owners one +1, two 0, three or more -1; service records mentioned +1; "no accidents" or accident free +1, an accident, collision, damage or claim mentioned -1; original, unrestored, survivor, numbers matching +1, restored or refinished 0 (shown, not scored), project or needs restoration -2 and tier 4; a modifications field or aftermarket, modified, swapped, lowered, custom words -1, unmodified or stock +1; title clean +1, salvage, rebuilt, branded, flood, lemon, parts only -3 and tier 4; TIER: a hard negative is 4, else score 4 or more is 1 (Concours), 2 or 3 is 2 (Excellent), 0 or 1 is 3 (Good), below 0 is 4 (Fair); Untiered when fewer than 3 signals are seen and no hard negative. Search check: no public page touched.

So the 290 s is not proven; the likeliest reading is the database under load at 08:22Z (an ingest and sweeps were running) holding each scan to its cap across the warm's list, but I have no log of it. WHAT I FOUND AND FIXED INSTEAD (each reproduced in the check, each fails on the base code): (a) mrNorm keeps letters and digits only, so "4¼ Litre", "4½ Litre" and "4 Litre" were one cache key and one typed-model match in archiveResolveToken (a 4½ answer served for a 4¼ and the reverse); fractionSig now keeps the fraction in the key and in the match (mrNorm itself untouched: the 1964½ Mustang reads through it). (b) THE REAL DEFECT, CLASS-WIDE: titleHasToken judged the token's edges with \b, and \b needs a word character beside the edge, so a model whose first word ENDS in ½ ("4½", "6½") never matched "1928 Bentley 4½ Litre Tourer"; the receipts check then called every pool of those cars with enough sales a swapped pool and refused it (invariant_failed). On production those Bentleys are all under the sale minimum (not_tracked), so nobody saw it; the first 4½ or 6½ pool that reached the minimum would have been refused. Edges are now judged by the letter beside them (same reading for every token that begins and ends with a letter or digit). CLASS SWEEP: the curated models with a fraction are 4½ Litre, 6½ Litre and 4½ Litre Supercharged (the Blower); the check lists them from lib/vehicleData.js and fails if one has no pool in the check (4½, 6½ and 4¼ now do). (c) The title read has ONE time budget for all its phrases (TITLE_READ_BUDGET_MS 6000, env.titleReadBudgetMs): it starts no scan past the budget, aborts the one in flight, answers null, and does not cache a read that ran out of time; a scan that never matches ran its full cap before. warmResolveCheck now has the three Bentleys (4¼, 4½, 8 Litre, plus 6½) with a 3000 ms bound per query (a slow read fails the check, not a 290 s warm), a scan-budget test (fetch delayed 2.5 s, budget 1.2 s: stops at 1.2 s; 7.5 s on the base code), and a 4¼ versus 4½ cache test. The rows were stamped with the live epoch at the moment of the write (warmwhy now: both rows stored under storedEpoch 2026-11-06T15:00:05.718Z, expired; the Bentley 4¼ row stored 08:22:47Z Nov 7 under that same epoch) and the daily ingest then bumped the epoch at the END of its run: ops ingestlog shows job_ingest ending 13:58:13Z Nov 7, 15:00:05Z Nov 6, 15:27Z Nov 5, 15:24Z Nov 4, 15:05Z Nov 3, 17:01Z Nov 2 (the live epoch is 2026-11-07T13:58:13.400Z; warmDay: 18,855 of 20,303 stored rows read mismatch, the rest were stored after the bump). A deploy does not move the epoch (only scripts/ingest.js bumps it, after a run that inserted rows), and the warm and the reader both read the one app_config row through currentEpoch. So a warm run in the hours before the day's ingest ends is stale at that bump by design (Sam's epoch-match rule), however fresh it is when written. FIX AT THE CAUSE, TWO PARTS: (a) the warm tasks (warmDemo, warmBuy, warmMC) now carry epochNote in their reply: the epoch they stamped, the last bump, the usual bump window from the last 7 job_ingest events, and aheadOfBump with the sentence "Run the warm after today's ingest" (lib/warmDay.js warmEpochNote; reads the log, writes nothing); (b) a real stale-stamp path: currentEpoch keeps the last known value when its poll fails (right for a reader), and epochForWrite stamped that value: a warm instance that saw E1, whose app_config read then failed after ingest bumped to E2, stamped E1 on a row computed against E2, a fresh row that reads stale. A writer now stamps only a value the last poll confirmed; after a failed poll it reads the row itself and, if that fails too, stores nothing (stored_row_no_epoch_refused, as for an unreadable epoch). The reader is unchanged. I did NOT make the warm refuse to run before the ingest (the ingest end is not signalled anywhere; adding a marker means editing the nightly ingest job): if you want that, it is a small change to scripts/ingest.js (an app_config marker for the run) and I will do it on your word.   1) THE WARM DECLINES BEFORE THE DAY'S INGEST. scripts/ingest.js writes app_config ingest_done (an ISO time) at the end of a run, AFTER the epoch bump, and not for a run that stopped at its request cap; lib/warmDay.js warmGate/warmGateFor read it; the ops tasks that WRITE warm rows (found by scanning the source: warmMC, warmDemo, warmDemoCheck, warmBuy, warmLive) answer, before writing anything, { refused: "ingest_not_done", writes: 0, line, doneAt, via } when the marker is not today's UTC day. THE LINE: "The warm did not run: today's ingest (UTC 2026-11-08) has not finished. The last finished run was 2026-11-07T13:58:13.000Z. A warm now would be stamped with the previous epoch and read epoch_mismatch at the ingest's bump. Run it after the ingest ends, or add force=1 to run it anyway." An unreadable marker also refuses, with its own line; force=1 runs it. Until the first run after this ships writes a marker, the newest job_ingest event stands in for it (via: ingest_log), so the gate works from the first call. TWO THINGS YOU MUST KNOW (not asked, found): (a) CRON CALLS BYPASS THE GATE. vercel.json schedules warmDemo at 00:05 and 12:05 UTC, warmDemoCheck every 15 minutes, and warmBuy parts 1 to 6 at 00:10 to 01:21 and 12:10 to 13:21 UTC: ALL of those run before the ingest ends (13:58 to 17:01Z), so every row they store reads epoch_mismatch at the bump by the same cause. A gate on them would switch the schedule off, which is your decision, not this rule's. If you want them moved, the times to move to are after the ingest event (about 17:30Z) or to run them as the ingest job's last step. (b) Last turn's warmEpochCheck passed warmBuy for the wrong reason: my wiring put epochNote on warmBuy's early "stopped" return, not its final reply; fixed here and the check now reads the LAST return of each block.

  EXAMPLE: 1999 Porsche 911 Carrera 996 manual coupe, 61,400 miles, no tier picked.
  desk.evidence (BUILT): { asOf:"2026-10-27", count:18, matching:24, median:37024, q1:34583, q3:37860, low:31500, high:37500, period:{from:"2026-04-03",to:"2026-10-27"}, latestSale:{date:"2026-10-27",price:39731,platform:"Cars & Bids"}, population:{sentence:"These are the sales of manual coupes."}, stale:{days:12,threshold:90,flag:false}, insufficient:false, sentence:null }. asOf = date of the latest completed sale IN the population; count = the population (what the meter draws); matching = every priced sale of the car before the population cut. stale.threshold = config DESK_STALE_DAYS (default 90); flag = (case date minus asOf) > threshold. market.meter IS this block (same count, low, q1 as p25, median, q3 as p75, high; sheetRead builds the meter from it). INSUFFICIENT (fewer than 3 sales, or fewer than 5 when a tier is picked, the engine's existing floors): { insufficient:true, sentence:"There are too few sales of manual coupes in Excellent condition from 25,000 to 55,000 miles to give a reference, 2 on record.", median:null, q1:null, q3:null, low:null, high:null, count:2 }, and market.meter is null. Never a 0.

Sorted close first, then by distance. relevance is decided from the verified year, generation (lib/modelRules.js), body, gearbox and miles distance, never from the model name: close = same year, same generation, same body, same gearbox, miles within the larger of 10,000 or a quarter; similar = same generation and body with the same or an unstated gearbox; a different generation or body is not listed. photo = the listing photo URL or null, never a placeholder. inPopulation:false for matching sales outside the population (Tiptronic when the subject is manual), kept in the list so the page shows them apart.
  desk.outside (stage 2): [{ label:"Automatic", count:5, median:31000, low:26500, high:34000, sentence:"Automatic cars sold for about $6,000 less than manual ones, 5 sales against 18." }], one entry per excluded group with 3 or more sales; nothing for a smaller group.

- VIN VS TYPED, WHY TWO VINS CAME BACK UNRESOLVED, AND A FIX, TIP FOR LANE C, READY B (Lane B, Oct 29): lane-b-e101-cold, code 6d439af0 (on 2e44f910); NOT pushed, no warm, no ingest, no production read or write for this stage (offline), stamp, SPEC_V and epoch unchanged. DOES THE REAL VIN FLOW ASK THE MODEL FIRST? Yes: api/sellerDecision.js resolves the VIN first (a partial decode returns the model question with chips, vinConfirm) and only then calls vinSearchPlan, which re-read the car's words ("1985 Jaguar XJ", "2002 Ferrari 550 Maranello") and gave up with "This VIN does not name a car whose sales can be read" unless that re-read came back valid. My harness (vintypedlive) built the VIN from the live listing's year, make and model without the question step, so the two unresolved cars are the re-read failing, and it fails the same way in the real flow after the model is confirmed: the XJ re-read asks which XJ (the live taxonomy lists XJ6, XJ12, XJS), and the 2002 Ferrari 550 Maranello re-read is invalid_vehicle because the curated production years of the 550 Maranello end at 2001 while the VIN proves a 2002 car exists.   2) MILEAGE WORDS. New top-level mileageWords beside mileageDelta: "4,000 more miles". Built from the SAME reading as the take (one delta, one formatter), present only when both readings are reliable and the reading WENT UP. A lower reading is never worded "fewer miles": an odometer does not run backwards, so a drop is a unit or typing difference between two listings and is treated as unreliable (no mileageDelta, no mileageWords, and the take names no direction), exactly as the Find card's take never says "fewer". No change in miles (delta 0) keeps mileageDelta 0 and has no words. Kilometres, a gap over 250,000 and a missing reading give neither. The take and the words can never disagree: takeAgrees() refuses any take that names a direction the words lack or differ from, and a candidate whose take and words disagree is rejected (take_mileage_disagree). One real case found and closed: a LISTED car whose latest earlier listing is not the record shown (it has no photo) would have worded one record and taken the tail from another; now the take carries no tail there. Words are a count and the word miles only: no valuation word.

Each batch read 8 NEW models (not the same 8: the memo prevented repeats; "models 8" every time because every batch met ~100 unseen models), wrote the rows of those 8, and left the rest waiting; the pause then doubled (4, 8, 16, 32 s) because slowness was judged on the SUM of row read + 8 model reads + write against 3 s. The measured requests were fine (read 565 to 1110 ms, a model read 235 to 373 ms, write 365 to 871 ms). Distinct models and rows in the untiered archive: NOT READ (no database key in my lane); the SQL above prints both.
  2 FIX: rows are taken MODEL BY MODEL; each model's quartiles are read once for the whole backfill (before, once per run, again every night); a read returns a batch of rows over several models (order=model,id inside a make), only a cut-off model is continued. Plain keyed filters, no OR. Rules unchanged. PROOF (scripts/tierSpeedCheck.mjs): the same tier AND the same evidence for all 2,400 sales as the old id-order job (frozen copy in scripts/fixtures/tierJobBefore.mjs); a run stopped at --max and resumed equals an uninterrupted run; a failed write then a rerun equals it too; every model read once; with 600 models the old job leaves sales waiting in one run, the new one tiers all 2,400.
  3 SLOW IS THE DATABASE'S: a batch is slow when its LONGEST SINGLE REQUEST (a row read, a model read or the write) exceeds --slow = 2500 ms (about 2.2 times the worst measured read, 1110 ms); the pause doubles, 3 such batches in a row stop the run, one request over 15 s stops it at once, every request still aborts at 6 s. Useful work no longer counts. Mutants: judged on the total again, slow never true, hard ceiling removed, a failed model read treated as no band: all killed. Fails closed: a failed read throws and writes nothing; a failed model read leaves its sales unstamped and the run says so.
  4 PRIORITY (lib/tierPriority.js): first the Desk's own pools, 81 make/model units from the 100 Hagerty comparison cars (27 makes: Porsche 911/356/930/928/944/964/993/996/997/991/981/Carrera GT/918/Cayman/Boxster, Ferrari 250/365/Testarossa/348/308/F430/550/488/458, Corvette, Camaro, Mustang, Chevelle, Mercedes SL and others), matched without case; then up to 300 of the most searched specs' models, ordered by the nightly recompute's own ranking (rankSpecKeysByViews); then every other model in make, model order. A run stopped early leaves those pools complete (tested). How many ROWS those hold: not read; the SQL gives the total, the job log prints rows per model visited.
  5 THROUGHPUT (simulated with the MEASURED latencies: read 840, model read 305, write 600 ms, batch 100, pause 2000; the id-order job under the same numbers stopped itself at 28 to 67 rows done, 71 to 170 a minute, matching Sam's run): new job, bandReads 20: 484 rows/min at 2 sales per model, 633 at 5, 967 at 20, 1,131 at 50. In the 70 minute cap that is 34,000 to 79,000 rows a night, so the 50,000 cap is reachable from about 5 sales per model; nights = ceil(untiered rows / 50,000): for 150,000 rows 3 nights, 300,000 rows 6. Real number: needs the untiered row and model counts from the SQL. Recommend: keep nightly max 50,000, batch 100 (a write of 100 rows measured 365 to 871 ms; larger writes are not worth the risk), pause 2000, bandReads default raised 8 to 20 (still one request at a time). To finish sooner, dispatch the same run by hand at a quiet hour; runs serialise (concurrency group).
  6 Checks: tierJobSafetyCheck (all existing assertions kept; only its fake PostgREST learned the new filters), tierAssignCheck (same, fake widened, assertions unchanged), tierWordsCheck, tierPoolCheck pass; new tierSpeedCheck registered in prePush, 8 mutants killed.

- REASON LINE TABLE (Lane B, Oct 28, e99-20261028-trimfix, lib/reasonWords.js; every producer builds its line there, no page writes one; check scripts/reasonWordsCheck.mjs). Before and after, one per line, [id | before | after]:
    thin.house_share | BEFORE: The sales of this car are too one-sided to mark a range from. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: These sales come mostly from one place, so no range is shown.
    thin.few_sales | BEFORE: Not enough sales of this exact car to give a reliable range. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: Too few sales to show a range.
    thin.mixed_prices | BEFORE: These sales sit in very different price ranges, so no typical range is shown. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: These sales sit in very different price ranges, so no range is shown.
    thin.pooled_apart | BEFORE: These sales split into options that sit in different price ranges, so no one typical range is shown. Pick an option below to read its own sales. | AFTER: These sales split into options priced apart, so pick one to see its range.
    thin.few_comparable | BEFORE: Too few of these sales can be compared side by side to give a reliable range. These are the sales on record. | AFTER: Too few of these sales match closely enough to show a range.
    wide.mileage | BEFORE: Wide because 20,000 to 90,000 miles. Add yours. | AFTER: The range is wide because mileage runs from 20,000 to 90,000 miles.
    wide.year | BEFORE: Wide because these run from 2008 to 2014. Pick a year. | AFTER: The range is wide because the cars run from 2008 to 2014.
    wide.mods | BEFORE: Wide because 4 of the 12 sales are modified cars. | AFTER: The range is wide because 4 of the 12 sales are modified cars.
    wide.none | BEFORE: These sell on condition and history more than mileage. Here are the twelve sales. | AFTER: These sales vary with condition and history more than with mileage.
    year.note | BEFORE: No 2010 sales in this range. These are 2008 to 2009 cars. | AFTER: No 2010 sales here, only 2008 to 2009 cars.
    year.none_of | BEFORE: None of these sales is a 2010; they are 2008 to 2009 cars. | AFTER: None of these sales is a 2010, they are 2008 to 2009 cars.
    option.floor | BEFORE: Convertible, 5 sales, too few for a range | AFTER: Coupe, 12 sales, too few for a range
    option.range | BEFORE: Coupe $20,000 to $30,000, 12 sales | AFTER: Coupe $20,000 to $30,000, 12 sales
    options.note | BEFORE: Each option's count is read over its own window, so the counts can add up to more than the headline count. | AFTER: Option counts use their own time spans, so they can add up to more than the total.
    mileage.note | BEFORE: Too few sales near 40,000 miles to narrow it. This is the range for all twelve. | AFTER: Too few sales near 40,000 miles to narrow it, so this is the range for all 12 sales.
    chart.caption | BEFORE: By quarter, November 2023 to September 2026. Quarters with fewer than 5 sales are left out. | AFTER: By quarter, 2008 to 2009, quarters under 5 sales left out.
    chart.window | BEFORE: The chart covers 33 months, the range the last 11. | AFTER: The chart covers 33 months, the range the last 11.
    mileage.band | BEFORE: 12 sales within 15,000 miles of 40,000, since December 2025. The band reads the last 12 months. | AFTER: 12 sales 2008 to 2009, since December 2025.
    window.line | BEFORE: 12 sales, since December 2025. | AFTER: 12 sales, since December 2025.
    window.longer | BEFORE: Based on 9 sales over the last 24 months. | AFTER: Based on 12 sales over the last 24 months.
    basis.one | BEFORE: Based on one sale, in March 2026. | AFTER: Based on one sale, in March 2026.
    basis.since | BEFORE: Based on nine sales since March 2025. | AFTER: Based on 12 sales since March 2026.
    basis.latest | BEFORE: Based on nine sales, the latest in March 2026. | AFTER: Based on 12 sales, the latest in March 2026.
    basis.pool_one | BEFORE: Based on one sale of 1995 911 Carrera, in March 2026. | AFTER: Based on one sale of 1995 911 Carrera, in March 2026.
    basis.pool_since | BEFORE: Based on nine sales of 1995 911 Carrera since March 2025. | AFTER: Based on 12 sales of 1995 911 Carrera since March 2026.
    basis.pool_latest | BEFORE: Based on nine sales of 1995 911 Carrera, the latest in March 2026. | AFTER: Based on 12 sales of 1995 911 Carrera, the latest in March 2026.
    latest.sale | BEFORE: Latest sale: March 2026. | AFTER: Latest sale: March 2026.
    includes.from | BEFORE: Includes sales from 2021. | AFTER: Includes sales from 2021.
    scope.typed | BEFORE: Showing the Coupe as named. | AFTER: Showing the Coupe as named
    scope.every | BEFORE: Showing every edition of this car. | AFTER: Showing every edition of this car
    scope.same_price | BEFORE: The editions of this car sell for about the same, showing every edition. | AFTER: The editions of this car sell for about the same, showing every edition
    scope.only_kept | BEFORE: Only the Coupe has three or more sales of this car, showing Coupe. | AFTER: Only the Coupe has three or more sales of this car, showing Coupe
    scope.none_kept | BEFORE: No edition of this car has three sales on its own, showing every edition. | AFTER: No edition of this car has three sales on its own, showing every edition
    scope.no_year | BEFORE: No 1974 sales yet, showing 1973. | AFTER: No 2010 sales yet, showing 1972 to 1973
    scope.few_year | BEFORE: Too few 2006 sales, showing 2005 to 2007. | AFTER: Too few 2010 sales, showing 1972 to 1973
    refusal.verify | BEFORE: Sam could not verify this one, so no figures are shown. | AFTER: No figures are shown because this car could not be checked.
    refusal.not_a_car | BEFORE: (new in e98: no line) | AFTER: This does not read as a car, so no figures are shown.
    refusal.varied | BEFORE: Sales too spread out for a range. | AFTER: These sales are too spread out to show a range.
    refusal.read_failed | BEFORE: The archive read did not finish. Try the search again in a moment. | AFTER: This could not be read just now, try again in a moment.
    refusal.no_body | BEFORE: The 993 911 was not sold as a Targa. If you mean a different body or a related model, tell me which and I'll pull the right sales. | AFTER: The 993 911 was not sold as a Targa, try another body or a related model.
    refusal.not_tracked | BEFORE: We haven’t tracked a 1995 911 Carrera sale yet. When one sells, it’ll show up here. | AFTER: No sale of a 911 has been tracked yet.
    refusal.no_sales | BEFORE: No sales of a 1995 911 Carrera are on record in the last five years, so there is no range to show. | AFTER: No sales of a 1995 911 Carrera are on record in the last five years, so there is no range to show.
    refusal.builder | BEFORE: Singer cars are not compared with standard 911s, so Sam shows no range for this car. | AFTER: Singer cars are not compared with standard 911s, so no range is shown.
    cold.still | BEFORE: Sam is still reading the sales for this one. | AFTER: The sales for this one are still being read.

- CHART LADDER, STAGE 1 AND THE FIELD SHAPE FOR LANE E (Lane B, Oct 28). STAGE 1: yes, it is computed at read time from the stored answer's own sales (rawPool, full rows with date and price) like matchedOption: NO stored answer change, NO stamp bump. One honest limit: the stored answer holds the window the answer reads (12, 24 or 36 months), not the wider 36 month chart set, so scoped candles need three candles of 5 sales of ONE option inside that window and will land less often than the pooled chart; dots land on everything else. Carrying the 36 month chart rows in the stored answer would land more candles but changes stored answers (a stamp decision, e100); I have NOT done it. FIELD SHAPE, on every result and thin answer as answer.chart (raw.chart), settled: chart = { type: "candles" | "dots" | "withheld", scope: null | { dimension, value, label, line }, size: "quarter"|"half-year"|"year"|null, spanLabel: string|null, caption: string|null, note: string|null, buckets: [{ period, label, low, high, typical, count }] | null, dots: [{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", price: 12345, option: "PDK"|null }] | null, withheld: { reason: "too_few", floor: 3, n, line } | null, n }. candles: draw buckets, caption under it, scope.line above it when scope is set (the engine's words: "The candles show the PDK sales only, 24 of the 31."); note is the held-chart sentence ("The mix of cars changed from quarter to quarter, so a change here would not show the market moving.") and prints under the chart when present. dots: draw one dot per sale, date against price, option names each dot (null when the answer has no options), caption "Each dot is one sale, since December 2025.", no line between dots, no trend. withheld: draw nothing, print withheld.line ("Only 2 dated sales, too few to chart, so the sales themselves are listed."). Too few = under 3 dated sales. Pages print these fields and compute nothing; the old d.trend, d.chartCaption and d.trendHeld stay on the answer unchanged.

- VIN VS TYPED, WHY TWO VINS CAME BACK UNRESOLVED, AND A FIX, TIP FOR LANE C, READY B (Lane B, Oct 29): lane-b-e101-cold, code 6d439af0 (on 2e44f910); NOT pushed, no warm, no ingest, no production read or write for this stage (offline), stamp, SPEC_V and epoch unchanged. DOES THE REAL VIN FLOW ASK THE MODEL FIRST? Yes: api/sellerDecision.js resolves the VIN first (a partial decode returns the model question with chips, vinConfirm) and only then calls vinSearchPlan, which re-read the car's words ("1985 Jaguar XJ", "2002 Ferrari 550 Maranello") and gave up with "This VIN does not name a car whose sales can be read" unless that re-read came back valid. My harness (vintypedlive) built the VIN from the live listing's year, make and model without the question step, so the two unresolved cars are the re-read failing, and it fails the same way in the real flow after the model is confirmed: the XJ re-read asks which XJ (the live taxonomy lists XJ6, XJ12, XJS), and the 2002 Ferrari 550 Maranello re-read is invalid_vehicle because the curated production years of the 550 Maranello end at 2001 while the VIN proves a 2002 car exists. DOES THAT MAKE TYPED AND VIN DIFFER? Yes: typed gave a question or an 'invalid year' answer, the VIN gave a dead-end line that says the VIN names no car, for a car the flow had already accepted. FIX (lib/vinAsTyped.js vinSearchPlan): when the re-read is not valid the VIN's own year, make and model stand and the typed path runs on them (no vin or chassis in the typed vehicle); a VIN with no year, make or model still says so; a valid re-read still wins. CLASS: every VIN whose car's words the resolver does not return as valid (a question, an invalid year, a timeout). CHECK scripts/vinPlanCheck.mjs (in prePush): question, invalid year, timeout, no vehicle, valid wins, no model still unresolved, the real Ferrari 550 Maranello through the real resolver; 5 FAIL on the old function, all pass now; vinTypedCheck passes. STILL TO COME ON THE NEW BUILD (PUSHED B-ENGINE 2): the 458 Speciale Aperta proof (vintypedlive now takes ?match=<title fragment> and ?repeat=3: the typed path three times and the VIN path three times, each computed fresh, the order of the first twelve cards each time, the first differing card between runs, and the fields that differ), the failed-texts warmwhy (docs/warm-failed-texts.txt, 8 a call), and the two sweeps (refusals, bodynames). I did not guess any clause from those two. (a) Buy API license and contract before production on a public page: NOT ALLOWED until approved. "The use of eBay's Buy APIs in production is intended for eBay partners only." "You must apply for production access through the eBay Partner Network." "Users must meet standard eligibility requirements, get approvals from eBay support organizations, and sign contracts with eBay." "There is no guarantee that your application for production use of the APIs will be approved." And from api_call_limits: "Buy APIs require an additional license." The requirements page does not mention a Production keyset at all, so a keyset alone is not shown to be enough: UNCONFIRMED that the keyset Lane D used is approved for production use; I would hold further production calls until Sam hears from eBay. (b) Storage, caching and refresh: UNCONFIRMED, and so NOT ALLOWED to store. The requirements page is silent ("no rules on data storage, caching limits, or refresh frequency"); the rules sit in the license agreement, which refused reading. (c) Display rules, from the requirements page (written around partner checkout; whether they bind a listings page is UNCONFIRMED, treat as binding until eBay says otherwise): "The image of the item must be an eBay image." (applies to Find: no re-hosted or substitute photos). "Show the eBay logo." (applies). "You can show a shortened version of the full title" with the full title on hover; DE: "Full title required." (applies). "Shipping costs must always be called out separately. Even if it is free shipping." (applies). "Partners and users are not permitted to sort items." (CONFLICT with Find if eBay rows are ranked or interleaved by our order; eBay rows would have to keep eBay's order, in their own block.) "Required: Only surface FIXED PRICE items." (CONFLICT: Lane D's plan B polls auctions, 3,603 open auctions; auctions would not be allowed.) "You must indicate when the item is not new." "Filter delivery country for domestic market." Feeds and being paid for sales need joining the eBay Partner Network. Whether a listings page must carry it once approved: UNCONFIRMED. A lower reading is never worded "fewer miles": an odometer does not run backwards, so a drop is a unit or typing difference between two listings and is treated as unreliable (no mileageDelta, no mileageWords, and the take names no direction), exactly as the Find card's take never says "fewer". No change in miles (delta 0) keeps mileageDelta 0 and has no words. Kilometres, a gap over 250,000 and a missing reading give neither. The take and the words can never disagree: takeAgrees() refuses any take that names a direction the words lack or differ from, and a candidate whose take and words disagree is rejected (take_mileage_disagree). Recommend: keep nightly max 50,000, batch 100 (a write of 100 rows measured 365 to 871 ms; larger writes are not worth the risk), pause 2000, bandReads default raised 8 to 20 (still one request at a time). To finish sooner, dispatch the same run by hand at a quiet hour; runs serialise (concurrency group).
